feedback.summary: The strategy reads like a team-values poster, not an instruction set: it has no buy thresholds, no map/site logic, no utility or pace rules, and no adaptation triggers. It never caused a clearly wrong call, but it also never prevented the economy spiral (eco at $19,000 in d3, eco at $22,350 in d5) or the repeated standard setup that the opponent's fakes and executes beat. It is consistent and harmless, which is exactly why it scored 3-13.
strengths: Consistent and non-contradictory: every call can be traced to one of the five bullets, so the AI never got conflicting guidance.
Correctly emphasizes team-wide buys and trading, which is the right high-level philosophy for CS economy.
Mentions not repeating yourself, which is the right instinct for a game that punishes predictability.

mistakes.what: Chose eco with save utility while holding $19,000 — far more than a full buy — throwing away a round and the loss bonus compounding.
mistakes.md_issue: 'Buy as a team and keep your money together' says nothing about when a buy is affordable; there is no full-buy cost or per-player threshold, so the model guessed 'can't afford full buy'.
mistakes.fix: Buy rule: full buy whenever team money ≥ $21,000 (T) / $23,000 (CT) or every player has ≥ $4,700; eco only when team money < $10,000; otherwise half-buy. Never eco above $15,000.

mistakes.what: Eco'd again at $22,350, gifting another round and letting the opponent's economy snowball to 0-5.
mistakes.md_issue: 'Play aggressive when you feel it, careful when you don't' gives no rule for losing streaks; nothing says 'stop saving when you can already full buy'.
mistakes.fix: If team money ≥ full-buy cost, buy full regardless of score. If down 3+ rounds, force/half-buy at ≥ $12,000 rather than eco — never eco two rounds in a row above $15,000.

mistakes.moment: d6–d12 CT side, repeated standard_2_1_2 / stack calls
mistakes.what: Standard setup was used in 8 of 12 CT rounds; the opponent's fakes and executes beat standard repeatedly (they won 10 CT-side rounds).
mistakes.md_issue: 'Don't repeat the same thing too much' is unquantified and has no counter-move; there is no rule mapping opponent tendencies (fake_a_go_b, execute_a) to a setup (retake_a, stack_a).
mistakes.fix: Track opponent's last 3 T rounds. If ≥2 were fakes, use retake on the faked site. If ≥2 were executes into site X, stack X. Never use the same setup more than 2 rounds in a row; after 2 repeats, switch to the counter.

mistakes.moment: d13–d16 T side, force/eco/full with default_mid and split_a
mistakes.what: Forced at $4,000 (pistol, fine) then forced at $8,350 (d14) and eco'd at $10,350 (d15), then full-bought only at 3-12 — economy never stabilized on T side.
mistakes.md_issue: No T-side economy ladder and no plan-selection rule; 'Use your utility to help the team' doesn't say which utility fits which plan (smokes for executes/splits, flashes for rushes).
mistakes.fix: T economy: pistol = kevlar+pistol; if team money < $10,000 eco with no utility; $10,000–$18,000 force with Galil/MAC-10 + armor; ≥ $21,000 full buy with smokes+flashes. Plan: default_mid vs unknown, execute/split into the site they stacked least, rush only vs aggressive_mid.

suggestions: Replace values with numbers: every buy, utility and pace rule should have a dollar threshold or a count ('≥ $21,000', 'last 3 rounds', 'never twice in a row').

Encode the game's actual mechanics: name the setups (standard_2_1_2, stack_a, retake_b), the plans (execute_a, fake_b_go_a, default_mid) and the utility tiers, so the model picks from the real option set instead of inventing intent.

Write explicit if/then adaptation rules tied to the SITUATION block: 'if opponent's last 3 rounds include ≥2 fakes → retake the faked site', 'if we lost 3+ in a row and can afford full → full buy, no eco'.

Add a short economy ladder per side (pistol / eco / force / half / full with thresholds) and a rule that forbids eco'ing when a full buy is already affordable — this alone would have changed d3 and d5.

feedback.summary: The strategy is well organized and its core reads (stack → hit the other site, standard → split/fake) are correct and clearly stated, which carried a 13-3 win. Its main weaknesses are economic: the buy thresholds are too conservative and the pistol-round rule contradicts itself, so the team left money on the table and mislabeled buys. Adaptivity is decent but the anti-predictability rules are vague ('rotate every round') and sometimes conflict with the read-based rules.
strengths: Clear priority ordering and a readable structure with concrete plan names and win percentages.
Correct core reads: stack → hit the other site, standard → split/fake, retake → execute into the given site.
Explicit anti-predictability section and a predictability check using your own last calls.

mistakes.moment: d1 R1 T pistol, $4,000 team money
mistakes.what: Called buy 'half' on the pistol round; the rule says pistol is a full team buy, so the label and the rule disagree.
mistakes.md_issue: 'Half start / OT: $800 start — pistol round is a full team buy (armor + pistols + utility)' conflicts with the T buy rule 'Full if team avg ≥ $4,000', which produced 'half'.
mistakes.fix: Add a pistol-round override: 'Pistol round (R1/R13): buy = full (armor + pistol + utility) regardless of the money thresholds; never label it half.'

mistakes.what: Called 'force' on the CT pistol round, again contradicting the pistol rule and the CT threshold.
mistakes.md_issue: CT buy rule 'Full if avg ≥ $4,200' plus no pistol override means the pistol round gets mislabeled and the buy logic is ambiguous.
mistakes.fix: Add: 'Pistol round override applies to both sides: buy full (armor+pistol+utility) even if below the normal full-buy threshold.'

mistakes.moment: d14 R14 CT, $18,200 team money, enemy broke
mistakes.what: Forced with SMGs/armor instead of full-buying while rich against a broke opponent.
mistakes.md_issue: 'Force ≥$2,800 only vs their eco' is too permissive: it lets a rich team force instead of full-buying, and the economy section says 'Full-buy > force > eco, always'.
mistakes.fix: Rewrite: 'If team avg ≥ full-buy cost, always full-buy — even vs their eco. Force only when avg is between $2,500 and the full-buy cost AND they are on eco/force.'

mistakes.moment: d8/d11 T, repeated execute_a into a B-stacking opponent
mistakes.what: Hit A repeatedly on the same read; the anti-predictability rule was overridden by the stack read without a check.
mistakes.md_issue: 'Never repeat the same T plan ... unless it's a hard counter to a confirmed read' is vague about what counts as confirmed and gives no tie-break when the read and the anti-repeat rule conflict.
mistakes.fix: Add: 'If the same plan was called last round, require a tendency ≥65% AND a fresh observation this round to repeat it; otherwise switch site or plan type.'

suggestions: Give every buy rule an explicit override order (pistol > full-buy affordability > force window > eco) so labels can't contradict each other.
Tie numeric thresholds to the actual full-buy cost shown in the situation block instead of fixed dollar figures, so the rule scales with side and round.
When two rules can conflict (read vs anti-predictability), state which wins and the exact condition for the exception.
Make anti-predictability operational: track last 2-3 calls per side and name the concrete fallback plan when a repeat is blocked.

preview: Challenger brings a loose, vibes-first playbook — buy together, trade together, mix it up and enjoy the ride — while Bot Analyst arrives with a full scouting report, economy tiers, and a matchup table for every read. The collision point is discipline versus improvisation: Bot Analyst wants to punish the most recent pattern and never repeat a setup, while Challenger's unpredictability could scramble those reads if the team stays genuinely varied. Watch the economy: if Bot Analyst's buy rules keep it fully equipped while Challenger's crew drifts into half-buys, the analyst's structured defaults and anti-predictability will grind out rounds — but if Challenger's aggression lands early picks and breaks the script, the analyst…

analysis.headline: Bot Analyst's adaptive reads crush Challenger's static buys
analysis.text: The turning point came early: Bot Analyst's .md forced a read-based plan from round two onward, alternating split and fake sites while Challenger's instructions only ever said 'buy as a team and keep your money together' — a solid economy rule with no tactical read attached. That let Bot Analyst punish Challenger's predictable standard_2_1_2 and stack setups repeatedly, building a 9-3 halftime lead that Challenger never recovered from. The lesson for prompt writers: a rule that tells the agent how to adapt to the opponent beats a rule that only manages resources — give your agent a read-and-react instruction, not just a budget policy.

md:
# Play Simple, Play Smart

- Buy as a team and keep your money together.
- Play aggressive when you feel it, careful when you don't.
- Stick with your teammates and trade kills.
- Use your utility to help the team.
- Don't repeat the same thing too much.
- Stay calm and have fun.

# Read, Punish, Rotate — Never Give Them the Same Round Twice

## 0. Priorities (in order)
1. **Economy discipline.** Never force broke. Full-buy > force > eco, always. Save when <$2,500 each and no kept rifles.
2. **Exploit the read.** The situation shows their tendencies and last rounds — counter the *most recent* pattern, not the average.
3. **Stay unpredictable.** Never repeat the same T plan or CT setup twice in a row unless it's a hard counter to a confirmed read.
4. **Play the matchup table.** Pick the plan whose row beats their likely setup.

## 1. T-Side Rules
**Buy:** Full if team avg ≥ $4,000 (or ≥$3,400 with kept rifles). Force only if ≥$2,500 each AND they're on a save/eco. Eco if <$2,500. Plant every eco (the +$800 loss bonus matters).

**Plan selection (default_mid is your anchor, ~40% of rounds):**
- **They stack a site** (tendency shows stack_a/stack_b, or 3+ CTs seen there): hit the *other* site. `execute_other` or `fake_their_site_go_other` (fake into a stack = 75%).
- **They play standard_2_1_2** (most common): `split_a/b` (58%) or `fake_a_go_b` (62%). Alternate sites.
- **They retake_a/retake_b** (give a site away): `execute` into the given site (65%) or `default_mid` (60%). Do NOT rush it.
- **They play aggressive_mid** (lots of mid presence, early picks): `rush_a/b` (70%) — their sites are empty. Or `default_mid` slow.
- **They're on eco/force:** `rush` the weak site fast; don't over-invest utility.
- **No read yet (first 2 rounds):** `default_mid` then `split` opposite site.

**Utility:** Full utility on executes/splits/fakes/default_mid. Rushes: flashes only (2-3), skip smokes.
**Pace:** default unless countering aggressive_mid (fast) or stacks (slow default_mid).
**AWP:** true if affordable and you have a rifle core; false on rushes/ecos.

**Anti-predictability:** Track your own last 3 T calls. If you've hit A twice, go B or fake. If you've defaulted twice, execute.

## 2. CT-Side Rules
**Buy:** Full if avg ≥ $4,200 (CT full costs more). Force ≥$2,800 only vs their eco. Save otherwise. Buy kit when ≥$4,500.
**Setup selection:**
- **They rush** (tendency rush_a/b, or fast rounds): `stack` the rushed site (70% for them = you win). `standard` loses to rushes.
- **They execute/split** (most common): `standard_2_1_2` is safest; `retake_x` if you read the site (execute into retake = they win 65% — avoid unless certain).
- **They fake a lot:** `standard` beats fakes (62% T = you lose 38%, acceptable); don't over-rotate. `retake` on the faked site is punished.
- **They default_mid:** `stack_a/b` (68% for them = bad) — instead `retake` the site they favor, or `standard` + aggressive mid info.
- **They're on eco:** `standard`, hold angles, don't over-extend. AWP mid.
- **No read:** `standard_2_1_2` round 1, then adjust.

**Utility:** `heavy` vs rushes and site hits (biggest swing). `normal` default. `save` only on eco.
**AWP:** true on standard/retake (mid control, long angles). False on stacks vs rushes (close fights).

**Anti-predictability:** Rotate setups every round. If you stacked A last round, play standard or stack B. Never retake the same site twice.

## 3. Economy & Momentum
- **Loss streak:** after 2 losses you're at $2,400+ bonus — that's a force window *if* they're also weak. Otherwise save one more.
- **Win streak:** keep full-buying; don't get greedy with saves when ahead.
- **Half start / OT:** $800 start — pistol round is a full team buy (armor + pistols + utility). OT $10,000 = full buy every round, no saving.
- **Kept weapons:** if 2+ rifles survive a loss, force next round even at low money.

## 4. Reading the Situation Block
- **Their last 3 rounds on this side** = strongest signal. Counter the *latest*.
- **Tendencies %** = base rate. If a tendency >60%, hard-counter it; if split 50/50, play your default and stay unpredictable.
- **Your own last calls** = predictability check. If you've been readable, break the pattern this round even at slight EV cost.
- **Enemy estimated money:** if they're broke, expect eco/force — play standard, don't stack (they'll rush your weak side). If rich, expect full execute — stack or retake-read.

## 5. Two Short Examples
**Example A (T, 5-4, we have $4,200 each, they've stacked B last 2 rounds, tendency stack_b 65%):** Don't hit B. Call `fake_b_go_a` with full utility — fake into their stack, execute the empty A. 75% win. Next round, if they rotate to A, switch to `execute_b`.

**Example B (CT, 8-6, they rushed A twice, tendency rush_a 60%, we have $4,500 each):** `stack_a` with heavy utility and AWP off (close fights). Their rush walks into 3 CTs. If they then slow down, next round `standard_2_1_2` and AWP on mid.

## 6. Golden Rules
- One read per round; commit to the counter, don't hedge.
- Never eco with a rifle core alive.
- Never repeat a plan/setup back-to-back without a confirmed read.
- When lost, default: T `default_mid`, CT `standard_2_1_2`.
- Plant on every T eco; buy kit on every CT full buy.
